title: room for improvement, use it a lot
content:
I use this app a LOT because it's a way to manage purchases and tracking across lots of vendors, without subjecting myself (and the vendors I buy from) to Amazon's predatory practices.

There's room for improvement, but I will say that search has improved a bit over the last year, and more retailers I like are showing up.

Biggest drawbacks are if you purchase using shop pay and there is a problem with not actually ever receiving your purchase.  Shop doesn't insure that their merchants actually exist, and provides no easily accessible customer support.  However, if you pay using the installment options on Shop Pay, you can go to the third party company that provides that financing, and submit a claim.  In all cases, adding the word "fraud" to your conversation with the chatbots can be very productive.

content:

After thinking about it more, I’d like to offer a 40% refund to your original payment method if you keep the bags. This way, you don’t have to worry about the high cost and inconvenience of returning them, and I hope it helps ease the frustration you’ve been feeling.

I feel like a fool. I was duped. Learn from my mistake. Do not buy from this company.

content:
I initially tried this app because I thought it would be a good package tracker. The tracking functionality without letting the service access my email account was ok. I hope this company didn’t mean to exclude other races or promote one color as superior to others. But that’s what the marketing looks like. The only way to defeat systemic racism is to deny racist behavior and it’s supporters. So I deleted this app.

author: tankerace

title: Has great potential, but it could be a lot better with a couple of tweaks
content:
I like the concept of this app.  I will keep it for a while, in the hopes there will be some updates to make it even better.  That’s why i gave it 4 stars... for now.

Two tweaks I would recommend be added, sooner, rather than later.  They will keep me using the app while I wait for the issues get fixed:

1) add a “nickname” function.  Make it at the first visible place where I check my status (and make it populate the notification, too).  I buy a lot online, so I like to be able to know at a glance WHICH order this status is for.

2). Add a DELETE function at the top level, not just “delivered” and “archive”.  Once it’s delivered, I frequently don’t need to have any more update reminders.

Parts of the app work great (capturing most of the pertinent details from emails, good visual dashboard).

Parts of it are confusing without some additional guidance (either a separate manual, or hints & tips onboard).  I could guess at some, (how to get the requested action to show up on he screen,) but not others. (Couldn’t figure out how to make the edits stick; the update button doesn’t seem to keep the edited data.)

And parts of it don’t cleanly connect the requested action at all levels.  Example: when I request to delete an item on the list at the “view all items” level, that delete doesn’t appear to propagate to all iterations of the same tracking number, or even to views of the same data from the “all shippers” level.  Also, it does not appear to update the list until I do a swipe down motion to refresh the screen.  If you already have to refresh the next level up screen when you go back to it, why not use the updated info to refresh it?

title: Not updating from carrier feed
content: I don’t understand why people are so thrilled with an app that doesn’t update delivery status often enough. The carrier has had multiple updates yet the app still has the initial shipment status and its’s been over a day. For a package that is supposed to arrive in less than 48 hours from the time it was shipped, not updating means the app provides me with zero information. It is essentially a list of tracking numbers vs a shipment tracker. I could do this in Notes or even Notepad. Unless you’ve got hundreds of shipments going to your gmail that you want the app to list automatically, this app is fairly useless as once it lists them it doesn’t update the status. Suggest they come up with some method to make some money to get funding for the development team. The UI is really good, but with the basic functionality essentially non-existent I can’t rate it low enough. Was really hoping to use Arrive over Deliveries as the app looked great, but I got fooled by the looks. Headed back to Deliveries.

title: Deleterious
content:
I am absolutely disgusted with this app. The tracking is a waste of time, no better than just using tracking emails sent from the individual online shops. The Shop Cash idea is great until you try to use it; using it always messes up your order and you get overcharged. 2/3rds of the personalized suggestions are for marijuana or vape products. Several times, when using my Shop Cash (which can only be done through the app), the merchant accepts the order, then it gets “lost” during shipping, or, after ten days or so, the merchant tells me the item is out of stock and cancels the order.

This time, the app gave the merchant an old and deleted billing address as the shipping address. Of course, the package was lost. So, it will cost the merchant a second shipping charge to get the package to me and make the package arrive too late for its intended purpose, the merchant will have to issue me a refund, or I will lose my money and potentially be pushed to file fraud charges. What a frustrating waste of time for both buyer and merchant.

title: Wants access to my Gmail account? No thank you!
content:
First of all, I was asked to download this app in order to track the shipping on my order. but once I finally got it all set up, all it showed me was that my order had, in fact, been ordered... 😒 No shipment status or tracking info whatsoever.

I’m usually pretty comfortable with sacrificing small portions of my online privacy as a trade off for convenience. But wanting to read all my emails in order to track my shopping habits? That seems like gross overreach, and instantly made me skeptical of everything else about this app.

author: CircusTrap

title: Used to be good
content:
Shop used to be a really good package tracking app, but now it’s more about advertising than tracking. Before, I could click on a map and see where my package was; now I can only do that near the end of its journey. Before, it was easy to see all my expected deliveries; now I have to figure out which place to click in order to see them—it has to go to a different page rather than being there when I open the app. I don’t enjoy all the ads when I open the app, it’s distracting and cluttered, and makes it hard find my packages.
I really want my maps back, where I can easily see where my packages are, even if they are still at the place I ordered from and not moving yet. I don’t want to click on my package and see this: “visit business website.” If I wanted to do that, I wouldn’t need Shop.
Please return the app to its original, useful, easy-to-use, uncluttered design. I’m ready to cancel it because it’s so useless now.

content: This has so many good reviews because of how convenient it is. But it’s a huge problem if you link your email to them. Just don’t do it. Go to your Google account, then third party permissions under security and make sure they don’t have that access. If they do block them. And I know people will say “I don’t care, I have nothing to hide.” Doesn’t matter. It’s the principal. It’s a slippery slope

content: Seems like about 1/2 the time, the tracking info is correct, while the other 1/2 of the time, it’s so far off I need 2 maps to “track them”... Items that show up as being “In Transit” may actually be “In Transit”, while a few arrived months ago, & others are “Unknown”; the Sending Tracking # shows an item left Asia & is arriving via the Australian Postal Service, while others are in a state of “We know it left, & was last tracked to leaving Shanghai, but while it should’ve been Arriving at Chicago O’Hare, it went to New York, & SHOULD be Arriving @ your destination 12 weeks ago, but the USPS can’t verify WHERE it is, or went, when it left New York; the only thing that we ALL know is that it’s still in ‘Location: None’, & should arrive at my location on ‘Date: Unknown’. The tracking numbers have “disappeared” from USPS’ lists, so “no one knows where it is, or when, (or IF), it’ll ever get to (me).” Before the local P.O. was “temporarily closed until further notice”, things were always ahead-of-, or on-schedule, I damaged; ever since the USA’s U.S.P.S. “Temporarily” closed the local P.O. (> a year ago), the items, from small packets to large packages seem to arrive “if”, instead of “when”, & most parcels, regardless of size or packaging, which DO arrive, are damaged in some way; sometimes they look like a 737 ran over them, & others only have superficial abrasions & similar “cosmetic damage to only the packing”, with some arriving in “pristine” condition, & others are closer to “Does anyone know what this looked like BEFORE it left its origination point?”, requiring photos for proof of damage & a refund being issued, while I’m still in need of the good-working-condition item I’d ordered. Getting 3 items from the same order go through 1) Australia, 2) Canada, and 3) someplace I can’t pronounce, but starts with a letter “K” & ends with “stan”, & a dozen letters in-between without ANY vowels, makes me wonder why they didn’t all go into the same mailer & Take the same route, (since they all came from the same place at the same time)...

title: Not Great
content:
I was excited to use the Shop app because it was advertising a great promotion on a jewelry item I had been wanting to purchase. Unfortunately, my experience was frustrating. The item required personalization, but the Shop app would not allow me to customize it within the app and instead redirected me to the jewelry company's website.

While the retailer's website still used Shop for checkout, payment, and order tracking, the promotional discount that initially attracted me was no longer applied. This created a confusing and disappointing customer experience, as the promotion seemed unavailable simply because personalization required completing the purchase through the retailer's site.

The app is useful for tracking orders and discovering products, but I hope Shop improves the integration between promotions and merchant websites so customers can receive advertised discounts regardless of where the checkout process is completed

title: Too many scams
content: I have ordered about 5 things from Shopify and have only received 3 of the 5 items I ordered.  Never order from Bombonds ( back support bras) as they will take your money and never deliver the product.  I can’t remember the other company but they sell castor oil packs, take your money and never deliver the product.  Also I ordered some quasi face masks but it was supposed to be a single order and I saw today that they just charged my credit card today for a monthly “subscription” that I never signed up for!  Keep your money safe from Shopify or they will find loopholes to charge your credit card monthly for “subscriptions” you never signed up for.  I also ordered from Resilia for a one time purchase that Shopify turned into an unauthorized subscription.  I was able to cancel my subscription but still had to pay for the product that they shipped out without my permission.  Too many sneaky little robbers here.  Beware!

title: Forced to download this app just to track an order
content:
One of 2 things is going on here:

1. When you order from a site that uses Shopify, they use their UI to trick you into thinking you HAVE to download the app to track your order, when in reality you’ll get tracking info from the seller (probably in an email) once the order is shipped.

2. This Shop app is the only way to track your orders from sellers that use Shopify.

I believe #1 is what’s going on, as you can’t expect every buyer to have a mobile phone and download and use their app.

But either way they deserve this 1 star review.
And once you download the app, they try their hardest to make it seem like you need to enable push notifications in order to track your orders… the entire experience just feels malicious (coming from a being developer myself).

The app itself is buggy too, when I first installed it, it let me skip signing in, skip all the notification stuff, etc. I was able to browse around, and when I decided to log in, I went to the account tab, and there’s a field to enter your email to log in or sign up. But as soon as I click on it, I get an error toast about “my passkey” and I lose focus on the text input box. If I click the input box again, same thing happens. I had to find the button to sign out, even though I was never signed in in the first place, then it put me through the whole new user flow again, where I was able to successfully sign in.

Overall, this is probably the worst user experience I’ve ever had trying to simply get the tracking information from a site I ordered some clothes from.

I’ll definitely delete the app as soon as I get what I need.

title: App Is ok - Support Is Not
content: Look, Shop belongs to Shopify and their App works as good as you’d expect for a Shopify app to work. It is basically an attempt to copy what eBay and Etsy already do, but with it’s own niche services. The problem with Shop/Shopify and their app is the third-party nature of their relationship with their sellers. It took me 20 days to get an order and the seller would not respond to inquiries. In fact, I never once heard from the seller. When I reached out to Shop/Shopify for help, they immediately recused themselves from the situation, denied any wrong doing and immediately insisted I get in touch with the seller. “Hello, I wouldn’t have reached out to you if the seller would have had any communication with me, or bothered themselves with answering just one of my emails.” Shop/Shopify is nothing more than a different, not so popular version of Etsy or eBay, with less customer service and more shade!

title: SHOP/SHOP PAY is where it ends
content: The app itself is fine, it allows you to track shipments/previous orders, etcetera, which is great when the majority of shopping is done online. Where I live there’s little option to shop local beyond groceries and household essentials (toilet paper, Kleenex, hand soap) SHOP is all about being carbon neutral, or so it claims, but nothing says HOW they do that. What I do know is that if you order something and use SHOP you’re looking at a 2+ month out delivery while your money is taken immediately. Companies “create” labels creating a record of moving product, but ACTUAL shipment dates are weeks/months past when an item begins moving. No more SHOP for me, I’ll order company direct and receive my shipments in a reasonable time for the products I buy.

title: Honest Review of the Shop App
content:
I love how convenient the app is and how it keeps all of my purchases in one place. That part works beautifully.

However, the package tracking feature is incredibly frustrating. I want to see an estimated arrival date and real time tracking, but instead I usually get a single notification that a label was created… and then nothing. No updates, no progress, and sometimes the next notification comes hours or even days after the package has already arrived.

At that point, I have to go to the actual product provider’s website just to get accurate information. For an app that’s supposed to simplify tracking, that’s pretty disappointing.

author: Eddiee :D

title: Deceptive App
content:
Shop, owned by Shopify, set up an app in the guise of a marketplace, but takes no responsibility for the sellers they partner with.

Recently I made a purchase completely within the Shop app. I found an item I was looking for from a store that had a storefront on Shop. I did my due diligence and looked over their website (link provided on the Shop app), policies, and reviews, then finally decided to make the purchase through the Shop app. I received confirmation of my order in the app and via email.

After a week of waiting for an update on my order, and hearing nothing from the Shop app or the website, I decided to investigate. I clicked on the store from my order in the Shop app and nothing, the storefront had disappeared, as well as their website and social media presence. I contacted Shop immediately and was told that they only track shipments and that they are not responsible for any order placed through their system, and that I would have to contact the seller directly (their contact emails were fake and pinged back to me) and/or to contact my method of payment.

No refund, no responsibility. My question, and one all Shop users should be asking, if Shop/Shopify takes a percentage of sales made using their systems, shouldn't they share in a percentage of the responsibility for their sellers? And if not, should they even exist?

content: I’ve been ordering from them about 2 years. I had a 40lb order of wax go unfulfilled for months even though it was in stock. Don’t fall for the false advertising. I ordered 12 sample bottles and 5 16oz bottles of fragrance. All 5 of the larger bottles were sample sizes. And all thrown in a single bag. Oils spilled out and covered everything. Just be prepared to check every item of every order every time. After about 30 orders, I assure you, most will be wrong. I also wrote them for over a month an a half asking about their custom fragrance service, they’ve ignored my questions I’ve sent several times over the last two months or that they need to “talk to Charlotte” or something and then never get back to me. Horrible follow up.

title: Worth it. Very helpful
content:
I was hesitant to download another app to add to my collection, especially an app that tracks. I could easily track it through whatever company it’s being sent by, right? Of course.
I downloaded it anyways & I am so thankful I did. Not only does it show you where your package is, it’s literally shows you on a map. I can see how my 1 little package has traveled half way across the world before it arrives at my door. I can zoom in & out & follow the exact route their taking. Below the map it types out the route which includes the country, state, town & times. I personally love this app. I think it’s very helpful & it keeps me intrigued with what’s really going on around me. Win win.

So happy with this app I recommend it to everyone!

title: Needs a Serious Overhaul
content:
The Shop app has been nothing but a headache. I recently ordered from two different brands and both used Shop for tracking. The user interface feels outdated and clunky, making it frustrating to navigate. Updates are slow, and it takes forever to get accurate shipping information — even when waiting months for limited drops from vendors.

For an app that’s supposed to streamline tracking and improve the shopping experience, it does the opposite. It desperately needs a complete redesign with faster, more transparent updates. Until then, it’s hard to recommend.

I’m actually quite surprised it has a 4.8 rating in the App Store.

Shop could not have handled this issue more poorly.

title: Absolutely useless for tracking my order.
content:

Absolutely useless for tracking my order.

I downloaded the Shop app specifically because the merchant’s confirmation email directed me there to track a $299 purchase I had already paid for. Instead of immediately giving me useful shipping information, the app pushed me toward setting up Shop Pay and entering payment information for future purchases.

After skipping that, Shop did locate my order, but the tracking information simply says “Waiting for details.” No carrier. No tracking number. No estimated shipping date. No meaningful explanation of where my order actually is.

If an app is being promoted as a way to track an existing purchase, then track the purchase. I should not have to navigate payment-service onboarding just to discover that the tracking service has no tracking information.

The order itself was placed weeks ago. Shop can apparently tell me that I spent $299, what I purchased, and where it is supposed to be delivered, but it cannot tell me whether the product has actually shipped.

That makes the tracking feature essentially useless to me.

I didn’t download Shop to shop. I downloaded Shop because I was told it could tell me where the product I already bought is. It couldn’t.

⭐ 1/5
